title: Safeguarding and escalation
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain the purpose and limits of safeguarding and escalation
Apply the principle to a service-business situation

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body:
Learning outcome
By the end of this lesson, demonstrate the ability to recognise and report safeguarding concerns while respecting the approved service plan, site procedures and limits of the cleaning role.

Workplace procedure
Be alert to immediate danger, unexplained environmental hazards, coercion, neglect indicators or threatening behaviour without attempting to diagnose or investigate. Record only directly observed facts and the person’s own words when relevant. Follow the organisation’s safeguarding and mandatory-reporting procedures applicable to the service and jurisdiction. If someone is in immediate danger, use emergency services and the site emergency plan. Do not promise secrecy or confront a suspected perpetrator.

Decision boundaries
Before acting, confirm authorisation, hazards and the person responsible for escalation. If the task exceeds training, consent, safe access or agreed scope, pause the affected work, protect others as appropriate, report promptly and document the reason. Never substitute an improvised method for a required specialist procedure.

Worked workplace example
A cleaner notices a blocked exit and hears a client say they feel unsafe. They ensure immediate safety within their competence, record the exact statement and notify the safeguarding contact promptly.

Guided practical exercise
Review four scenarios involving possible neglect, a privacy concern, an immediate threat and an ordinary housekeeping issue; classify urgency and draft factual reports.

Assessment and feedback
An assessor should observe a complete demonstration and confirm: Distinguishes emergency from routine escalation, records facts without speculation and protects the person’s privacy. If a critical safety, privacy or consent step is missed, provide targeted feedback and require reassessment before signoff.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Watch for immediate danger, unexplained environmental hazards, coercion, neglect indicators or threatening behaviour, without trying to diagnose or investigate.
If someone is in immediate danger, use emergency services and the site emergency plan first.

Pause the affected work if the task exceeds your training, the consent given, safe access or the agreed scope, and protect others as appropriate.
Record only directly observed facts and, where relevant, the person's own words.
Follow the organisation's safeguarding and mandatory-reporting procedure for the service and the jurisdiction, and report promptly.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: Only directly observed facts and the person's own words are recorded, without speculation.
Emergency and routine concerns are separated, and emergencies go to emergency services first.
The safeguarding and mandatory-reporting procedure for the jurisdiction is followed.
No secrecy is promised, and a suspected perpetrator is not confronted.
summary: The cleaner watches for immediate danger, coercion, neglect indicators and threatening behaviour, without trying to diagnose or investigate.
Only directly observed facts and the person's own words are recorded, and the organisation's safeguarding and mandatory-reporting procedures are followed.
Immediate danger goes to emergency services, and the cleaner never promises secrecy or confronts a suspected perpetrator.

knowledgeChecks.question: What observable actions demonstrate that you can recognise and report safeguarding concerns?
options: Investigating the concern yourself and confronting the suspected person and questioning the family
Promising the client that what they say will stay secret and writing their words on a sticky note
Recording directly observed facts and the person's own words, then following the safeguarding procedure
Diagnosing neglect from the appearance of the home and deciding what to do about it alone

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do about a safeguarding concern during a visit?
options: Keep the cleaning going and mention it to a colleague later and finish the room first
Remove the person from the area yourself and take them to the car park before the family arrives
Pause the affected work, report promptly to the designated contact, and document the reason
Decide alone whether the concern is serious enough to report and wait to see if it happens again

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say to record about a safeguarding concern?
options: Only directly observed facts and the person's own words when relevant
